metaDescription: Five portable chargers for iPhone compared on fast charging, built-in cables, magnetic attachment and size, from a 5000mAh magnetic pack to a 10000mAh 45W bank.
introParagraphs: iPhone owners have a few more choices than most, because recent models use USB-C, older ones still use Lightning, and many want wireless magnetic charging. This lineup covers that range: the Anker with a 30W USB-C cable built in, the INIU with a detachable cable and 45W output, the podoru 5000mAh magnetic pack, the VRURC with four built-in cables, and the HETP 2-pack of tiny 5200mAh banks with a built-in USB-C connector.

Capacity differs sharply. The Anker, INIU and VRURC are 10000mAh, with the Anker listing about 2 full charges for an iPhone 15, while the HETP and podoru are smaller at 5200 and 5000mAh and trade capacity for pocketability. Speed varies too: the INIU lists 45W, the Anker 30W, and the VRURC and podoru 22.5W and 20W.

We evaluated each pick from specs, listed features and buyer feedback rather than hands-on testing. Check your iPhone's connector, since the HETP is built for USB-C models, and for magnetic charging, use a MagSafe-compatible case. If you fly, keep banks in your cabin bag and note that all five are well under 100 watt-hours.

products.name: Anker 10000mAh 30W Power Bank
products.description:
The Anker is the most dependable all-rounder for iPhone owners. It delivers 30W through USB-C, twice as fast as a basic 5V/3A charger, and its listing says it boosts an iPhone 16 Pro Max to 50 percent quickly. The 10000mAh battery offers up to 2 full charges for an iPhone 15.

A 5.4 inch built-in USB-C cable is rated to endure over 10,000 bends, a durability claim that most budget banks do not make. It also accepts USB-C input, so you can recharge it with the same cable you use for your phone. The tradeoff is that the built-in cable is short and cannot be replaced, and the Anker sits at the highest price tier here.

It measures 4.32 by 2.58 by 0.98 inches, small enough for a pocket or purse. Compared with the INIU, it is slower but has a built-in cable, and compared with the podoru, it holds twice the capacity. Choose it if you want a trusted brand and USB-C iPhone compatibility.
products.bestFor: USB-C iPhone owners who want a trusted, durable, fast bank.
pros: 30W USB-C charging, twice a basic 5V/3A charger
Built-in cable rated for over 10,000 bends
Up to 2 full charges for an iPhone 15
cons: Built-in cable is short and not replaceable
Highest price tier of the five

products.name: INIU 10000mAh 45W Portable Charger
products.description:
The INIU is the fastest bank in this guide, listing 45W output that boosts an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 76 percent in the time quoted. It is 40 percent smaller and lighter than comparable banks thanks to a high-density battery. Flight-safe labeling adds confidence for travelers.

Its 0.4 foot detachable USB-C cable is replaceable, unlike the built-in cord on the Anker. The tradeoff is that you must carry that cable, and a short cord is a bit awkward when the phone is in your pocket. It sits in the middle of the price range.

At 10000mAh it is about 37 watt-hours. Compared with the Anker, it is faster and cheaper but has no built-in cable, and compared with the VRURC, it is much quicker though it lacks the extra cables. Choose it if speed matters.
products.bestFor: People who want the fastest top-up for a recent iPhone.
pros: About 40 percent smaller than comparable banks
cons: Short 0.4 foot cable is awkward in use

products.name: podoru 5000mAh Magnetic Power Bank
products.description:
The podoru is a magnetic power bank that snaps to the back of an iPhone, so there is no cable to fumble with. It has a 5000mAh battery and 20W PD fast charging, with a stronger magnet and nano adsorption designed to hold it in place. It is ultra-slim, so it does not make your phone unwieldy.

The listing recommends using it with a MagSafe case or no case to get enough suction, and a non-magnetic case will weaken the hold. The tradeoff is capacity, since 5000mAh gives about one charge, and it sits at the lowest price tier. It is a top-up, not a full backup.

It shines for walks and errands when you do not want a cable. Compared with the Anker, it holds half the capacity but removes the cord, and compared with the HETP, it is wireless instead of plugged in.
products.bestFor: iPhone owners who want a cable-free magnetic top-up.
pros: Snaps on magnetically, no cable needed
cons: Needs a MagSafe case or no case to hold well

products.name: VRURC 10000mAh 22.5W Power Bank
products.description:
The VRURC is the multi-cable bank, with three output cables and one fast-charging input cable all built in. It supports 22.5W charging, which the listing says takes a phone to 60 percent in 30 minutes. It can power up to 4 devices at once.

Recharging takes about 2.5 hours through the built-in USB-C input at 18W. The tradeoff is that built-in cables cannot be replaced, and 22.5W is slower than the INIU or Anker. It sits at the second-lowest price tier.

It is a good fit for travelers who share the bank with a partner or carry an Android device as well as an iPhone. Compared with the Anker, it has more cables but is slower, and compared with the HETP, it has more capacity.
products.bestFor: iPhone owners who also charge other devices and want cables built in.
pros: Four built-in cables, nothing extra to carry
Charges up to 4 devices at once

products.name: HETP 2-Pack 5200mAh USB-C Portable Charger

specList.label: Size
specList.value: About the size of a lipstick

products.description:
The HETP is a pair of tiny banks, each about the size of a lipstick, with a built-in USB-C connector that plugs straight into the phone. It is designed for iPhone 17, 16 and 15 series, which use USB-C, and for Android phones with USB-C. No cord is needed.

The listing warns that phone case thickness matters, so a thick case can stop the connector from seating. The tradeoff is capacity, since 5200mAh is about one charge, and an older Lightning iPhone will not work. It sits at the second-highest price tier for a two-pack.

Two banks let you keep one in a bag and one in a coat. Compared with the podoru, it plugs in instead of snapping on, and compared with the Anker, it is far smaller but holds half the capacity.
products.bestFor: USB-C iPhone owners who want tiny, cordless backup banks.
pros: Two lipstick-sized banks in the pack
Easy to tuck into a pocket
cons: Thick cases can block the connector
Does not work with Lightning iPhones

buyingCriteria.explanation: Recent iPhones use USB-C, while older ones use Lightning. The HETP plugs directly into USB-C and will not work with a Lightning phone. The Anker and INIU use USB-C cables, so a Lightning phone needs a cable adapter. Confirm your connector before buying.

The INIU lists 45W and the Anker 30W, while the VRURC and podoru list 22.5W and 20W. A phone only charges as fast as it accepts, so a higher number is not always faster. USB-C PD spans 18 to 100 W versus 5 to 12 W on typical USB-A. Use a short quality cable.
The podoru snaps on magnetically, so there is no cable. It recommends a MagSafe case or no case for enough suction. A non-magnetic case weakens the hold. Wireless charging is also slower than wired.
A 10000mAh bank is about 37 Wh, while 5000mAh is about 18 Wh. Usable output is roughly 77 to 83 percent of rated. The Anker offers about 2 charges for an iPhone 15. Smaller banks give about one.
The HETP warns about phone case thickness because the plug must seat fully. A thick case can block it. Remove the case or choose a cable-based bank. Test fit before relying on it.
Banks of 100 Wh or less go in the cabin without approval. All five here are well below that. Carry them in the cabin and look for printed Wh ratings. Check your airline.

howWeEvaluated.title: iPhone compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked connector types and wireless support. The Anker, INIU and VRURC use USB-C, the HETP has a built-in USB-C plug, and the podoru uses magnets. This is based on listed specs, not hands-on trials.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging speed
howWeEvaluated.description: The INIU leads at 45W, and the Anker follows at 30W. The most basic pick for speed is the podoru at 20W.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and size
howWeEvaluated.description: The Anker offers 10000mAh in a 4.32 by 2.58 inch body, while the HETP is the smallest at 5200mAh. Capacity matters for travel days.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cable convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at cables built in, detachable or none. The VRURC has four built-in, the Anker one durable built-in, and the podoru none. Convenience varies with habit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the price tier
howWeEvaluated.description: The podoru is the lowest-cost pick, the VRURC sits low, and the Anker is the premium option. Features such as magnets only earn credit if they suit how you carry your phone.

cards.label: Wired banks
cards.text: The Anker, INIU, VRURC and HETP charge faster and hold more. They need a cable or plug.

cards.label: Magnetic bank
cards.text: The podoru snaps to the back of the phone. It holds less and needs a MagSafe case.

howToChoose.note: Recommendation: choose wired for capacity and the podoru for convenience.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A printed Wh rating under 100 Wh and a durable cable. Carry in the cabin.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Anker 10000mAh 30W Power Bank has a built-in cable rated for 10,000 bends and about 37 Wh capacity.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a durable cable and trusted build in the Anker, or the fastest speed in the INIU.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need a quick top-up. The podoru and VRURC sit at the lowest tiers.

faq.q: How do I choose between these chargers for iPhone?
faq.a: Start with your connector and how you carry the phone. Pick the Anker for a trusted all-rounder, the INIU for speed, or the podoru for magnets. Match capacity to your day.
You do not need to spend much. The podoru and VRURC sit at the lowest tiers. Pay more for the Anker's durability or the INIU's speed.

faq.q: Will a bigger bank fast charge my iPhone?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The phone controls the speed it accepts. A 45W bank will not charge a phone faster than the phone allows. Use a short quality cable.

faq.q: Do magnetic chargers work with any case?
faq.a: No. The podoru recommends a MagSafe case or no case. A non-magnetic case weakens the hold. Wireless charging is also slower.

faq.q: Will a lipstick-size bank work with my case?
faq.a: Possibly not. The HETP warns that a thick case can block the connector. Remove the case or test before relying on it.

faq.q: Can I fly with these chargers?
faq.a: Yes, in your cabin bag. All five are well below 100 Wh. Check your airline for rules.
